subject: AICcmodavg package for model average in Puma occupancy of the Central Andes

messages.author: ce5532ce531740ac
messages.subject: AICcmodavg package for model average in Puma occupancy of the Central Andes
parts:
Regards to everyone!

This is my first post in this awesome group of wise people.

Recently I design eight models to estimate Puma occupancy within a protected area of the Central Andes, based on ten site covariates related both with the antropogenic and habitat features presented in the landscape.

In the AIC model selection procedure for the occupancy parameter, results shows that there are three candidate models with similar weights of deltaAIC(<2): m1, m3 and m4 respectively.

                                                                                                                          nPars    AIC       delta     AICwt     cumltvWt
p(ELEVATION+ CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(NDVI_MEAN)          6           137.98  0.00   0.25638     0.26        (m1)
p(ELEVATION+ CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(NDWI_MEAN)         6          138.28   0.30    0.22046    0.48        (m3)
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(POPDEN_MEAN)   6         138.50   0.52    0.19742    0.67        (m4)
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(ACCESIBILIY)        6          140.47  2.49    0.07371    0.75
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(ELEVATION)          6           140.64  2.66   0.06787     0.82
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(HFP)                       6          140.84  2.86    0.06138     0.88
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(CANOPY_MEAN)   6          140.84  2.86   0.06133     0.94
p(ELEVATION + CANOPY_MEAN + ACCESIBILITY)Ocu(EVI_MEAN)            6          140.84  2.86   0.06131     1.00
null_model                                                                                                          2          152.92 14.94  0.00015     1.00

How can I average these three models to get the weighted contribution of their individual parameter estimates? 

I was reading the Mazerolle's tutorial for this package and according to him, the function 'modavg' could be useful to model-averages the estimate of a parameter of interest among a set of candidate models, computes the unconditional standard error and the unconditional confidence intervals as described in Burnham & Anderson (2002).

Finally I want to assess the relative contribution of β coefficients estimated for each covariate.   

I'll really appreciate your help.

Cheers!

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] AICcmodavg package for model average in Puma occupancy of the Central Andes
parts:
Hi Juan Camilo,


If you want to assess the relative contribution of each variable in AICcmodavg, one way to do it would be to use the shrinkage estimator for model averaging (see ?modavgShrink). To use it, each variable should appear with the same frequency across your models. Also, note that there are issues of overestimating the magnitude of the effect with the natural average (modavg) to get model-averaged estimates for betas for variables appearing in models with low support (Cade 2015: Model averaging and muddled multimodel inferences. Ecology 96:2370-2382.). You also might want to standardize your explanatory variables.


Best,


Marc
